-- The stock body, captured before the name is shadowed. It is nil when no client data was -- sourced, and the call then says so rather than doing nothing. local refItemButtonOnEnter = ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter
function ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter(button) if not button then button = this end if not button then return end
-- Our keyring is a container, so its slot takes the stock general path's calls for a -- bag slot instead of the inventory-slot detour. if button:GetParent():GetID() == KEYRING_CONTAINER then if (button:GetRight() or 0) >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end GameTooltip:SetBagItem(KEYRING_CONTAINER, button:GetID()) ResetCursor() return end
if not refItemButtonOnEnter then message("benilla: Interface\\FrameXML\\ContainerFrame.lua was not sourced from the " .. "game data, so bag-slot tooltips cannot work. Check the client data path.") return end refItemButtonOnEnter(button) end
-- ══ The three bag verbs benilla answers differently ═══════════════════════════════════ -- Deviation: `OpenBackpack` opens every equipped bag, not only the backpack, so the -- vendor, bank, mail and trade windows that call it from OnShow bring up every bag to sell -- or deposit from; `CloseBackpack` is its inverse, `CloseAllBags` the unconditional form. -- The was-open memory is keyed by bag id because `ContainerFrame1..12` are recycled across -- bags, and every open and close goes through the stock `OpenBag`/`CloseBag`/`IsBagOpen`, -- so their guards and any addon that replaces them apply. BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN = {}
-- The unconditional close, from the stock ShowUIPanel's centre branch: it ignores the -- was-open memory and covers the bank bags, as the reference's CloseAllBags does -- (l.702-707). function BenillaCloseAllBags() for bagId = 0, (NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES or -1) do CloseBag(bagId) end end
-- A bag already open is remembered and left alone, so CloseBackpack leaves open a window -- the player opened; the reference's `backpackWasOpen`, one entry per bag. function BenillaOpenBackpack() for bagId = 0, (NUM_BAG_FRAMES or -1) do -- OpenBag's own test, repeated so the memory agrees with it: the backpack always, -- another bag only when its slot holds one. if bagId == 0 or GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) > 0 then if IsBagOpen(bagId) then BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] = 1 else BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] = nil OpenBag(bagId) end end end end
function BenillaCloseBackpack() for bagId = 0, (NUM_BAG_FRAMES or -1) do if not BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] then CloseBag(bagId) end end end
-- Published after the stock ContainerFrame.lua has loaded, so these are the definitions its -- callers reach (the stock `ShowUIPanel`'s `CloseAllBags`, a vendor's `OpenBackpack`). OpenBackpack = BenillaOpenBackpack CloseBackpack = BenillaCloseBackpack CloseAllBags = BenillaCloseAllBags
